high.title: Ringgit falls against US dollar, major currencies as Treasury yields rise
high.summary: The ringgit weakened to 4.0935/4.0975 against the US dollar, driven by rising US Treasury yields and investor focus on upcoming US labour market data. Key events including JOLTS, ADP employment data, and nonfarm payrolls on August 7 could further influence the ringgit's direction. This directly impacts Malaysian importers, exporters, and businesses with USD-denominated obligations.

high.title: Bursa retreats on cautious sentiment and profit-taking
high.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 4.56 points to 1,720.34 in early trading amid cautious sentiment and profit-taking, with market breadth turning negative as losers outpaced gainers. The retreat follows a one-week high supported by bargain hunting, with rising US Treasury yields weighing on sentiment. Malaysian investors should note the expected trading range of 1,710 to 1,740 this week amid global uncertainty.

high.title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against US Dollar Ahead of Key US Economic Data
high.summary: The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar, trading in a narrow range of RM4.07 to RM4.09, as Trump cancelled planned military strikes against Iran, easing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude surged 4.59% to US$88.10 per barrel amid West Asia conflict uncertainties. The US ISM Manufacturing PMI for July is due tonight, with markets watching closely for direction on USD strength.

high.title: Ringgit Ends Week Higher as Weak US Data Weighs on Dollar
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0835/4.0875 against the greenback, supported by weaker-than-expected US Q2 2026 GDP growth of 1.5% versus the 2.1% consensus estimate. The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, PCE, eased to 3.7% in June from 4.1% in May, reinforcing expectations for a September rate hike rather than immediate action. These macroeconomic shifts have direct implications for Malaysian trade, capital flows, and monetary policy outlook.

high.title: Bursa Ends Higher on Blue Chip Buying, Tracks Regional Markets
high.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 4.50 points to 1,724.90, buoyed by a return of foreign buying and positive regional sentiment, particularly South Korea's KOSPI surging 17.91% and Japan's Nikkei gaining 4.03%. The Bank of Japan's decision to hold interest rates steady was in line with expectations and contributed to regional market stability. The resumption of foreign inflows into Bursa Malaysia is a significant positive signal for domestic market confidence.

high.title: Bursa edges down as investors digest Fed decision
high.summary: The FBM KLCI opened lower at 1,714.42 and slid further to 1,712.88 as investors digested the US Fed's decision to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75%, with the broader market turning negative. US strikes on Iran following an attack on a US military base in Jordan added to downward pressure. The geopolitical escalation in West Asia poses significant risk to regional market stability.

high.title: Bursa's key index ends at an intraday high on continued buying support
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed higher driven by investor rotation into consumer and plantation stocks, diverging from weaker regional peers. The Fed held rates steady for the fifth consecutive meeting at 3.50%-3.75%, providing some market clarity. However, renewed US-Iran hostilities and rebounding crude oil prices continue to elevate geopolitical risk and near-term volatility concerns.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher as US Fed holds rate steady
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened marginally to 4.0850/4.0920 against the US dollar as the Fed kept the Federal Funds Rate unchanged at 3.50%-3.75%, causing the DXY to fall 0.57% to 100.842. The decision was not unanimous, with three voting members favouring a rate hike, signalling potential tightening ahead. The steepening US Treasury yield curve, with the 10-year yield rising 7 basis points to 4.68%, indicates tighter financial conditions globally.

high.title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against Greenback on Improved Local Sentiment
high.summary: The ringgit traded cautiously ahead of the US Federal Reserve's FOMC rate decision, hovering around RM4.08-RM4.09 against the US dollar. Malaysia's economy is projected to grow 4%-5% in 2026, likely towards the upper end, with manageable inflation despite energy supply shocks. Lower-than-expected US consumer confidence data caused US Treasury yields to dip, signalling the Fed may hold rates steady, with direct implications for ringgit direction and Malaysian capital flows.

high.title: Ringgit Ends Higher Against Most Currencies, Slips Versus US Dollar
high.summary: The ringgit slipped against the US dollar to 4.0885/4.0930 as markets awaited the Fed's FOMC meeting outcome on July 28-29, a key driver of currency direction. Global crude oil prices trended lower amid US-Iran negotiation hopes and potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, reducing near-term energy price pressures. The FOMC outcome and Middle East developments are critical watch points for Malaysian investors and businesses exposed to currency and energy markets.

medium.title: Amazon surges to more than US$3tril in market value for 1st time
medium.summary: Amazon crossed a US$3.1 trillion market valuation after posting quarterly profits of US$62 billion, driven by 37% revenue growth in AWS and AI-related divisions. This reinforces the broader AI infrastructure investment trend, with hyperscalers collectively spending US$700 billion on AI data centres this year. Malaysian investors exposed to technology and AI-linked stocks should take note of the sustained momentum in this sector.

medium.title: Maybank said to be near buying Ageas stake in Etiqa
medium.summary: Maybank is reportedly close to acquiring Ageas's 31% stake in Etiqa Insurance, with the deal potentially valuing the stake at US$1.2 billion and Etiqa's total valuation at approximately US$4 billion. The transaction could be announced as early as Monday and would give Maybank full ownership of one of Malaysia's largest insurers. This is a significant corporate event for Maybank shareholders and the Malaysian insurance sector.

medium.title: Bursa ends slightly higher on late buying in selected heavyweights
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed marginally higher after late buying in heavyweight stocks, despite regional markets ending mostly lower on AI spending concerns. Market sentiment was partially lifted by Trump's signals of Hormuz Strait negotiations, which caused Brent crude prices to fall and eased inflation concerns. Analysts expect the FBM KLCI to trade within the 1,710 to 1,740 range this week, supported by continued foreign fund inflows.

medium.title: Bursa Opens Mixed Amid Wall Street Gains, Geopolitical Concerns
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 2.04 points at opening to 1,718.36 despite Wall Street gains, as geopolitical tensions escalated with a drone strike targeting gas vessels at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta. Market breadth was positive with gainers outnumbering losers, suggesting underlying sentiment remained cautiously optimistic. The widening US-Iran conflict poses risks to global energy supply chains with potential downstream effects on Malaysian businesses.

medium.title: Ringgit Opens Higher as Weaker US Data Weighs on Dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0800/4.0885 at the opening as the US Dollar Index fell 1.01% to 99.864 following weaker US Q2 GDP data and moderating PCE inflation. Analysts noted the data supports the Fed's stance of keeping rates unchanged in the near term, reducing pressure on emerging market currencies like the ringgit. This provides a more stable outlook for Malaysian importers and businesses with USD-denominated costs.

medium.title: Ringgit ends mostly higher regionally, flat against US dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit closed flat at 4.0875/4.0930 against the US dollar following the FOMC decision to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75%, though the non-unanimous vote signals potential rate hikes at the September meeting. Analysts noted the outlook favours the US dollar in the near term, which could exert downward pressure on the ringgit. Malaysian investors should monitor the Fed's September 15-16 meeting closely for policy direction.

medium.title: Ringgit closes marginally higher ahead of FOMC outcome
medium.summary: The ringgit appreciated slightly to 4.0875/4.0915 ahead of the FOMC decision, with Asian currencies broadly range-bound amid market caution. Rising crude oil prices — WTI up 3.67% to US$82.17 and Brent up 3.79% to US$87.28 — driven by US-Iran military tensions added inflationary concerns. A hawkish Fed tone was flagged as a key risk factor that could strengthen the US dollar and weigh on the ringgit.

medium.title: Defensive Stocks Lift Bursa at Close
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 3.08 points at 1,715.56, driven by consumer products, services, and telecommunications stocks amid cautious market sentiment. Iranian missile strikes on US military facilities renewed Middle East geopolitical concerns, bringing energy security back into investor focus. Gainers outpaced decliners in the broader market, though turnover values remained modest at RM2.48 billion.

medium.title: Bursa Rebounds to Open Higher on Improved Sentiment
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 4.68 points to 1,717.16 at the opening bell on improved market sentiment, with gainers outpacing losers in the broader market. Malacca Securities noted that upside potential would be limited by a global tech rout, signalling selective sector performance for the session. The rebound reflects cautious optimism among investors balancing local positive sentiment against external headwinds.
